CHAPTER 12 · ABITUR · LINEAR ALGEBRA

CHAPTER 12 · ABITUR · LINEAR ALGEBRA · BASIC AND ADVANCED COURSE

Linear algebra

Raw materials become intermediate products, intermediate products become end products. Matrices work through the whole factory in one step. After that it is about money: what does one piece cost, what is left over, and does the stock work out at all?

COMPULSORY TASK 2MATRICES
WHAT IS TESTED
  • Reading matrices off the interdependence diagram
  • Calculating total requirements and raw material requirements
  • Costs, contribution margin, profit
  • Assessing overdetermined systems of equations
CHECK-IN: WHAT YOU NEED

What is the first component of $\begin{pmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}$?

$1 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 1 = 3$

How much do $3$ QU at €$2$ and $4$ QU at €$1$ cost, in euros?

$6 + 4 = 10$

$x + y = 5$ and $x - y = 1$. What is $x$?

Add: $2x = 6$

TOOLKITWHAT YOU NEED FOR THIS CHAPTER
KEY POINT · INTERDEPENDENCE

Total interdependence: $M_{RE} = M_{RZ} \cdot M_{ZE}$. The order follows the route through the factory.

Requirement: $\vec{r} = M_{RE} \cdot \vec{e}$ for the production vector $\vec{e}$.

Variable costs per piece: raw material costs, making the intermediate products and making the end products together.

Contribution margin: revenue per piece minus variable costs per piece. Profit: sum of the contribution margins minus fixed costs.

More equations than unknowns: solve two equations and substitute the solution into the remaining one.

TO REVISE
SYSTEMS OF LINEAR EQUATIONS AND MATRICESMathematics 11 · chapter 4MULTIPLYING AND INVERTING MATRICESMathematics 13 Advanced · chapter E2.1
TASK 1LEVEL I · REPRODUCING

1From raw material to end product

A company first makes the intermediate products $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ from the raw materials $R_1$, $R_2$ and $R_3$, and from these the end products $E_1$ and $E_2$. The requirement in quantity units (QU) is shown in the interdependence diagram.

State the matrices $M_{RZ}$ and $M_{ZE}$.

Columns are the intermediate or end products, rows the raw materials or intermediate products: $M_{RZ} = \begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 4\\1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$ and $M_{ZE} = \begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 3\end{pmatrix}$.

Calculate the total production matrix $M_{RE}$.

$M_{RE} = M_{RZ} \cdot M_{ZE} = \begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 4\\1 & 2\end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 3\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}5 & 5\\10 & 15\\4 & 7\end{pmatrix}$. Row 1, for example: $2 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 = 5$ and $2 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 3 = 5$.

The company plans $20$ pieces of $E_1$ and $30$ pieces of $E_2$. Determine the requirement of intermediate products and of raw materials.

With $\vec{p} = \begin{pmatrix}20\\30\end{pmatrix}$, $\vec{z} = M_{ZE} \cdot \vec{p} = \begin{pmatrix}70\\110\end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{r} = M_{RE} \cdot \vec{p} = \begin{pmatrix}250\\650\\290\end{pmatrix}$. Check via the detour: $M_{RZ} \cdot \vec{z}$ gives the same vector.

Describe the meaning of the entry $re_{22}$ of $M_{RE}$ in context.

The entry has the value $15$: for one quantity unit of the end product $E_2$, a total of $15$ QU of the raw material $R_2$ is needed — over both production stages together.

TASK 2LEVEL II · MAKING CONNECTIONS

2What the company earns

The raw materials cost $4$, $2$ and $6$ euros per QU. Making the intermediate products costs $12$ euros ($Z_1$) and $18$ euros ($Z_2$) per QU, making the end products $25$ euros ($E_1$) and $40$ euros ($E_2$) per piece. $E_1$ sells for $180$ euros and $E_2$ for $260$ euros. The fixed costs are $2\,500$ euros.

Determine the vector $\vec{k}_v$ of the variable costs per piece.

$\vec{k}_v = \vec{k}_R \cdot M_{RE} + \vec{k}_Z \cdot M_{ZE} + \vec{k}_E$ (all three as row vectors). $\vec{k}_R \cdot M_{RE} = (4\;\;2\;\;6) \cdot \begin{pmatrix}5 & 5\\10 & 15\\4 & 7\end{pmatrix} = (64\;\;92)$, $\vec{k}_Z \cdot M_{ZE} = (12\;\;18) \cdot \begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 3\end{pmatrix} = (42\;\;66)$. Together with $\vec{k}_E = (25\;\;40)$: $\vec{k}_v = (131\;\;198)$ euros per piece.

Calculate the contribution margin per piece for both end products.

$\vec{d} = \vec{v} - \vec{k}_v = (180\;\;260) - (131\;\;198) = (49\;\;62)$. $E_1$ contributes $49$ euros, $E_2$ contributes $62$ euros.

Determine the profit when $20$ pieces of $E_1$ and $30$ pieces of $E_2$ are produced.

$D = \vec{d} \cdot \vec{p} = 49 \cdot 20 + 62 \cdot 30 = 980 + 1\,860 = 2\,840$ euros contribution margin. Minus the fixed costs: $G = 2\,840 - 2\,500 = 340$ euros profit.

Assess: “$E_2$ brings the higher contribution margin per piece, so the company should only make $E_2$.”

It is not that simple. The contribution margin per piece says nothing about how many pieces can be sold and which raw materials are sufficient for them. $E_2$ uses clearly more $R_2$ per piece ($15$ instead of $10$ QU) — if $R_2$ is scarce, what matters is the contribution margin per QU of the bottleneck raw material, and that is higher for $E_1$, at $\tfrac{49}{10} = 4.9$, than for $E_2$, at $\tfrac{62}{15} \approx 4.13$.

TASK 3LEVEL III · EVALUATING

3The stock does not work out

The stock holds $250$ QU of $R_1$, $700$ QU of $R_2$ and $300$ QU of $R_3$. Production is to be planned so that all three stocks are used up completely. We are looking for the numbers of pieces $x$ of $E_1$ and $y$ of $E_2$.

Set up the corresponding system of linear equations.

$M_{RE} \cdot \begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}250\\700\\300\end{pmatrix}$, written out $5x + 5y = 250$, $\;10x + 15y = 700$, $\;4x + 7y = 300$.

Show that this system of equations has no solution.

From the first equation $x + y = 50$, from the second $2x + 3y = 140$. Substituting $x = 50 - y$ gives $100 + y = 140$, so $y = 40$ and $x = 10$. But then the third equation is not satisfied: $4 \cdot 10 + 7 \cdot 40 = 320 \neq 300$. The system is overdetermined and contradictory — there is no solution.

Determine what amount of $R_3$ would have to be in stock for the plan to work out, and state the corresponding numbers of pieces.

$320$ QU of $R_3$ would be needed. Then $x = 10$ and $y = 40$ is the solution of all three equations. With the actual stock of $300$ QU, $20$ QU of $R_3$ are therefore missing.

Assess the statement: “A system of linear equations with more equations than unknowns never has a solution.”

The statement is false. More equations than unknowns only means that the system is overdetermined; whether it can be solved depends on whether the extra equations fit the rest. That is exactly what part c) shows: with $300$ on the right-hand side there is no solution, with $320$ there is exactly one.

LOOKING BACKTHE IDEA AND THE TRAP

TASK 1 · FROM RAW MATERIAL TO END PRODUCT

Columns belong to what is made, rows to what is used.

Trap: the order in the product is not arbitrary: $M_{RZ} \cdot M_{ZE}$ is defined (number of columns $2$ meets number of rows $2$), but $M_{ZE} \cdot M_{RZ}$ is not. If you swap the factors, you notice it from the formats.

TASK 2 · WHAT THE COMPANY EARNS

First the costs per piece, then the contribution margin, finally the fixed costs.

Trap: the raw material costs must not go through $M_{RZ}$ alone. You need $M_{RE}$, otherwise the second production stage is missing.

TASK 3 · THE STOCK DOES NOT WORK OUT

Three equations, two unknowns: the third equation decides whether the plan works out.

Trap: if you solve only two of the three equations, you get $x = 10$ and $y = 40$ and take that for the answer. With an overdetermined system, the check in the remaining equation is part of the solution.

TESTTHE SAME IDEAS, NEW NUMBERS
ROUND 1

What is the first component of $\begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\0 & 3\end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix}1\\2\end{pmatrix}$?

$2 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 2 = 4$

One piece brings €$50$ in revenue and has €$38$ variable costs. What is the contribution margin in euros?

$50 - 38 = 12$

ROUND 2

With a contribution margin of €$12$, $100$ pieces are sold; the fixed costs are €$700$. What is the profit in euros?

$1200 - 700 = 500$

$x + y = 3$, $x - y = 1$, $2x + y = c$. For which $c$ is there a solution?

$x = 2$, $y = 1$ in the third equation: $c = 5$.
